acceptance: specy-road grind-session --status is a read-only mode: scope is --until NODE (seed with the node's own leaves; for every node added that is not Complete add its effective dependencies, a group dependency adding its leaves, each expanded the same way; a dependency Complete by RoadmapIndex.status adds its leaves as done and is not followed further; deduplicated by node_key), --under NODE (the subtree), both (the intersection of that until-closure and the under-subtree), or with neither the parent in work/.milestone-session.yaml as --under; with no scope it exits 2 naming --until, --under and start-milestone-session, and an unknown node exits 2 naming the id (no node M99). --status with --plan or --step, and --watch without --status, are argparse errors; no new top-level command and no persistent state. Accepted limit: the grind loop plans --under only and stops after it picks --until, so it can still run ready leaves under --under that --until does not depend on; status does not count those

Gate nodes are not counted. Each non-gate leaf in scope is in exactly one bucket, from the plan grind-session --plan computes (gather_session_plan(root, None) filtered to the scope), first match wins: done (Complete), cancelled, held (an open gate among its unmet dependencies whether or not the leaf is claimed, plan.gated being only the unclaimed ones, next step set-gate-status <GATE>; or claimed with review state escalated, fix_round_budget_spent or executor_blocked, a review policy change since the claim, or a live worker, live meaning worker_state.active_for_node (not failed or terminated; completed still counts), leased to human or flagged needs_person), active (claimed or In Progress, with its review state and live worker id, harness and state; a leaf in plan.finished_claimed stays active and its line says the feature tip is Complete and unmerged), ready, waiting (plan.blocked with reason dependency, with waiting_on), finished, awaiting merge (each leaf in plan.finished_unmerged: Complete on its feature branch, which the integration branch has not merged; not done and counted in remaining; maintainer, 2026-11-10), not pickable (unauthored, needs codename, with reason); totals include remaining = total - done - cancelled. Review state comes from one public review_state(root, node_id) extracted from handoff status's _node_status, run only for claimed leaves in scope; review_state does not call trial_merge, so handoff status of a conflicting leaf still reports the conflict and the status report has no trial-merge line; handoff status's output, JSON and exit codes are unchanged

The estimate uses, for each done leaf in scope, the earliest history_index event with kind status and to Complete, matched by the leaf's current node_key and not its display id (a completion before a renumber of that node_key counts; a different node now holding the old id does not), timed by the event's at (the author date): below 5 completions or under 24 hours from first to last it says not enough data, naming the count and the minimum; otherwise the overall rate (n-1)/(last-first) and the recent rate (completions in the 7 days before now / 7 days) give earliest and latest as ISO 8601 datetimes with offset, now plus remaining divided by the faster and by the slower rate; when the recent rate is zero latest is the string none at the recent pace and earliest is now plus remaining divided by the overall rate; the output states the method, its inputs (n, first, last, recent count, window, minimum) and that held and waiting leaves are assumed to clear at the past pace; now is a parameter tests pin

Decisions: open decision and human-action entries of the merged ledger (shared and local), in scope first with node, summary, why_now, options with effects, recommendation and reason, default if unanswered, needed_by and ledger, printed as recorded; open entries outside the scope one line each; pros and cons printed as not recorded, the decisions schema has no field for them; then each held leaf with its reason and the next step its record names (RCA prompt, fix-round budget next, executor blocked_on lines, review accept-policy <ID>, set-gate-status <GATE>, worker reclaim or status) and no options recorded (not a ledger entry). The command writes no option, pro, con or recommendation of its own; a missing recorded field is named under missing

Sessions, independent of the goal scope: open brainstorm sessions (work/brainstorm-*.yaml not moved to work/brainstorm-closed/, via brainstorm_session list_slugs and read_session) with slug, mode and idea count, an unreadable file named under missing without hiding the rest; and every live presence session (session_presence list_sessions live_only) with agent, branch, note word for word, expiry and stale reason. Presence records have no role field, so no session is classified as a planner; docs/grind-session.md names the convention session start --note 'planner: <topic>', and a role field is deferred to M23

Human-readable text by default, its header ending with last updated <local time>; --status --json prints one JSON object with keys generated_at (ISO 8601 with offset), goal, scope, totals, held, active, ready, waiting, not_pickable, estimate (method, inputs, earliest, latest, reason), decisions (ledger, ledger_outside_scope, held), sessions (brainstorm, presence) and missing. No network and no harness call: with the remote's remote.<name>.uploadpack set to a sentinel script, the sentinel never runs, and git status, HEAD, the registry and the ledger are unchanged (the history cache under .specyrd/cache/ is the only write, as specy-road history). Reads only product paths an adopter has (roadmap/, work/, .specyrd/), no toolkit-only path

--status --watch [MINUTES] prints the report, then again after each interval, each after a separator with its last updated line, until Ctrl+C (exit 0); with --json one JSON object per line. The interval is MINUTES, else the new optional git-workflow.yaml key grind_session_status_interval_minutes (integer >= 1, in git-workflow.schema.json and as a commented line in the template git-workflow.yaml, read with load_git_workflow_config), else 30; a non-positive or non-integer value exits 2 naming the flag or key. Sleep and clock are parameters; tests never wait

The bundled skills specyrd-orchestrate.md and specyrd-grind-session.md tell the coordinator to run specy-road grind-session --status with the grind's scope at the start of a grind and every grind_session_status_interval_minutes (default 30), and to post its text output to the chat unchanged, using the harness's scheduler or wake-up where it has one and otherwise the first turn after the interval; they say --watch is for a person's terminal and name no single harness's scheduler. A skill-text assertion in tests/test_decisions.py pins the paragraph

Tests in tests/test_grind_status.py cover the rows of the sheet test table on temporary repos with dated commits and a pinned now; the grind-session and top-level help goldens; docs/grind-session.md gains a section on --status (watch, the interval key, sessions, the planner note convention); docs/git-workflow.md lists the key; cli_usage.py's grind-session line names --status; CHANGELOG [Unreleased]. READY reports the wall time of grind-session --status --until M16.8.4 on sr/ (informational). Out of scope: the GUI status modal (M17.14) and PM decisions from it (M17.15), a session role field and a pros/cons schema field (M23), the handoff status rename (M16.4.3)
Estimated net line change (informational, not a gate): package about +250, tests about +340, docs and skills about +55
nodes.title: grind-session --status reports a goal's leaves by state, a completion range from history, and what waits on a person, read-only

acceptance: finish-this-task treats a leaf's human: criterion A# as decided only when roadmap/decisions.yaml as committed at the leaf branch HEAD or at the integration branch tip (read with git; the working tree and decisions.local.yaml do not count) holds a closed kind: human-action entry with node the leaf, criterion: A# (new decisions-schema field, pattern ^A[1-9][0-9]*$), decided_by: operator and channel terminal or pm-gui; a planning-sheet A#: line no longer counts. The refusal lists each undecided criterion, says a sheet line no longer counts, and names decisions add <NODE> --kind human-action --criterion A# and the two ways a person closes it. handoff status lists the same undecided ids from the same function (text line and JSON key human_criteria_undecided); the review gate's pass/fail, its exit codes and the reviewers' n/a rule for human: items are unchanged. Test rows: no entry, open entry, closed without channel, other node, other criterion, local ledger only, sheet line only, uncommitted entry, entry committed on the leaf branch, entry committed on the integration branch, entry closed through the PM GUI's answer path

decisions close <ID> on an entry with criterion refuses, writing nothing, when stdin is not a terminal, when SPECY_ROAD_ORCHESTRATION_ROLE is set to anything but exactly coordinator (review_override.role_refusal), or when git user.name or user.email is unset; there is no --yes or other non-interactive override. Otherwise it prints the node, the criterion's text and the answer, asks y/N, and on y closes the entry with decided_by: operator, channel: terminal (new channel enum value) and an answer ending (recorded by <name> <email>); any other reply writes nothing. The PM GUI's existing answer path closes such an entry unchanged (decided_by: operator, channel: pm-gui). decisions add --criterion A# is accepted only with --kind human-action and a node whose A# starts with human:, and refuses a second open entry for the same node and criterion; any caller may open one. Test rows: not a terminal, each refused role value, unset identity, reply n, reply y. The new --criterion option is declared by one tests/parity/command_map.yaml row (old: specy-road decisions add, new: specy-road decisions add --criterion), so the parity inventory test passes

decisions close closes every other decision and human-action entry in the ledger without a planning-sheet line (close_entry's sheet-line requirement and its refusal are removed; preferences and standing rules are unchanged). grind-session --status does not list a closed pm-gui entry that has criterion under gui_pending, since finish-this-task consumes it; other GUI answers keep today's pending rule. Test rows: close with no sheet line, close of a preference, gui_pending with a criterion entry and with an ordinary answer

Docs and prompts follow in the same change: docs/roadmap-authoring.md's acceptance row and the exception sentence of 'The executor never writes its own planning sheet' (the A#: case is dropped: a person's decision on a human: criterion is a ledger entry, not a sheet line); the acceptance description in roadmap.schema.json (template, sr/ and dogfood copies) and decisions.schema.json (template and sr/ copy); suggested_prompts/bootstrap-roadmap.md; docs/orchestration.md's decisions CLI paragraph; docs/pm-gui.md and docs/grind-session.md where the GUI answer is described; the decisions add and close help goldens; the decisions parent help: a tests/parity/command_map.yaml row (old and new both specy-road decisions) for its changed close line, and its golden tests/parity/golden/help/specy-road__decisions.txt refreshed; the upgrade dry-run golden tests/parity/golden/upgrade/rc3-dry-run.txt refreshed for the template roadmap.schema.json change (it gains the line `would write schemas/roadmap.schema.json`); and a CHANGELOG [Unreleased] entry saying existing sheet A#: lines stop counting, the finish refusal names the replacement, and no migration copies them (a copy would turn an agent-writable line into a person's record)

docs/roadmap-authoring.md states the honour-system limits beside the acceptance row, in the manner of docs/orchestration-review.md's 'What the gate cannot stop': a process in a pseudo-terminal with the role unset or coordinator, a direct call of the library close function, a hand-edited and committed ledger entry, or a process that can read the PM GUI's code can still record a criterion decision; the channel, the recorder identity and the commit that adds the entry make a forgery visible in review, not impossible
Estimated net line change (informational, not a gate): package about +60, tests about +90, docs about +15
